## Why the best teams win

The model trained on 256 knockout team-seasons to predict how far clubs progress in European competitions. Its performance is measured by a mean within-season Spearman correlation of 0.46 between predicted and actual stages, with an AUC for reaching the final at 0.72. The model achieved a Brier score of 0.098 compared to a base-rate guess Brier score of 0.103. While this represents an improvement over the baseline, the edge was not tested statistically, so it cannot be called significant or superior. In terms of identifying finalists, 46.7% of actual finalists appeared in the model's top 4 predictions for their respective season.

When analyzing which stats drive deep runs, style emerges as the most predictive feature set with a Spearman correlation of 0.41 and an AUC of 0.69. The pedigree-only set yields a Spearman of 0.28 and an AUC of 0.66, while results alone achieve a Spearman of 0.3 and an AUC of 0.72. Combining all features reaches a Spearman of 0.46 and an AUC of 0.72. The most important stat is Attacks per game with an importance of 0.25, followed by Goal difference per game at 0.201. Both are marked as robust. Long passes (% of passes) follows with an importance of 0.137 and Passes per game at 0.128, both also labeled robust. These four stats represent the strongest statistical associations for deep knockout runs in this dataset.

## Winners vs runners-up

Comparing group and league-phase stats between winners and runners-up across all finals reveals no statistically significant differences when applying a Holm-adjusted p threshold of 0.05. The analysis focuses on the first four sorted stats: Pre-season UEFA club coefficient, Fouls committed per game, Shots per game, and Pass accuracy. For Pre-season UEFA club coefficient, winners were higher in 13 finals with a mean difference (z) of 0.57, but the Holm-adjusted p was 0.111. In the case of Fouls committed per game, where lower is better, winners had lower values in 12 finals with a mean difference (z) of -1.13, yet the Holm-adjusted p remained at 0.181.

The third stat, Shots per game, shows winners were higher in 11 finals with a mean difference (z) of 0.79 and a Holm-adjusted p of 0.292. Finally, Pass accuracy saw winners higher in 12 finals with a mean difference (z) of 0.76 and a Holm-adjusted p of 0.422. Since all these p-values exceed the significance threshold of 0.05, no difference between winners and runners-up is significant based on this data. Other stats like Points per game and Goal difference per game show even higher p-values of 1.0. The data indicates that while certain style metrics predict deep runs generally, they do not consistently differentiate winners from runners-up in the final stage when looking at pre-final phase statistics.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Teams beaten (%)' figures say how many teams the club did better than on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where doing better means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Use 'significant' or 'significantly' only for a Holm-adjusted p-value comparison, never for other differences. Write plain markdown without tables.

Write 350-450 words of markdown in total, two paragraphs of about 100 words under each of exactly these two headings, in this order:
## Why the best teams win
## Winners vs runners-up

Explain which stats are associated with deep knockout runs and whether pedigree, results or style matters most, using the feature-set comparison. Say how well the model does by comparing its Brier score with the base-rate Brier score and stating what share of the finalists were in its top 4; the model's edge over the base-rate guess was not tested, so do not call it significant or superior. 'Importance' is the average size of a stat's push on the expected stage, in either direction. The model learns from the knockout team-seasons, using each team's group/league-phase stats. Report findings only: do not explain how SHAP or the model works. Only call a stat 'robust' if its robustness label is robust. Winners vs runners-up compares those same group/league-phase stats, not what happened in the final; discuss only the first four stats in that comparison (it is sorted from smallest to largest Holm-adjusted p) and say whether any difference was significant. Never call a winners-vs-runners-up difference significant unless its Holm-adjusted p is below the significance threshold in the facts.
